+
+// Note: These routines perform the read with a native endianness.
+func readUnaligned32(p unsafe.Pointer) uint32 {
+	q := (*[4]byte)(p)
+	if goarch.BigEndian {
+		return byteorder.BEUint32(q[:])
+	}
+	return byteorder.LEUint32(q[:])
+}
+
+func readUnaligned64(p unsafe.Pointer) uint64 {
+	q := (*[8]byte)(p)
+	if goarch.BigEndian {
+		return byteorder.BEUint64(q[:])
+	}
+	return byteorder.LEUint64(q[:])
+}

+// Copyright 2026 The Go Authors. All rights reserved.
+// Use of this source code is governed by a BSD-style
+// license that can be found in the LICENSE file.
+
+//go:build riscv64
+
+package maps
+
+import (
+	"internal/byteorder"
+	"unsafe"
+)
+
+// Note: These routines perform the read with a native endianness. riscv64 is
+// little-endian only, so the byteorder BE branch of the portable version is
+// dead here and omitted.
+//
+// On riscv64 the compiler lowers the byte-wise byteorder helpers to a
+// load/shift/or chain (plus a bounds check) of many instructions, because it
+// cannot prove the pointer alignment; memHashFallback pays this for every
+// 8-byte word it reads. When the source address is naturally aligned a single
+// native load (lwu/ld, which zero-extends) materializes the bit-identical
+// little-endian value, so take that path. The portable byte-wise path is kept
+// for misaligned addresses and stays correct on strict-alignment cores.
+func readUnaligned32(p unsafe.Pointer) uint32 {
+	q := (*[4]byte)(p)
+	if uintptr(unsafe.Pointer(&q[0]))&3 == 0 {
+		return *(*uint32)(unsafe.Pointer(&q[0]))
+	}
+	return byteorder.LEUint32(q[:])
+}
+
+func readUnaligned64(p unsafe.Pointer) uint64 {
+	q := (*[8]byte)(p)
+	if uintptr(unsafe.Pointer(&q[0]))&7 == 0 {
+		return *(*uint64)(unsafe.Pointer(&q[0]))
+	}
+	return byteorder.LEUint64(q[:])
+}
